comments.text: 6510 port data direction. The engine installs $2F in several paths including $14E3 and $279F.
6510 banking port. The engine selects $35 for the RAM engine with I/O and $36 when it needs the KERNAL.
Zero-based upper player index. The nested ranking loops at $A378 and $A37A start from it and decrement through player zero.
Zero selects live controls. $A1CF enters the demonstration with phase one and the scripted stick driver at $9705 advances through the later phases.
Shared arithmetic byte. $9E57 initializes it as the scorecard ranking pass's current rank and $9E6E–$9E80 advance the rank between passes.
Signed high byte of the first ball motion component. The acceleration at $3A49 adds a signed high increment and $3B8E uses its sign for integration.
High byte paired with $E6 in the second launch result. $38CE writes it and the ground contact path at $394B stores its reversed sign component.
High byte paired with $E7 in the launch calculation. The path at $3962 scales that component and stores its high result here.
Fractional byte of the lateral aim coordinate, updated with carries into $0D64.
Projected mask centre X in half-resolution units, set at $AE2F after shifting the projected X. $AE41 subtracts half the selected mask width from it.
Projected terrain mask centre Y plus one, stored at $AE32. $AE68 subtracts the vertical mask offsets from this value.
First view coordinate byte supplied to the rotation coefficient routine at $2B0D. Moving the saved golfer position updates it at $2AD3.
Second view coordinate byte supplied in Y by $2B0B. $2AD5 keeps the incoming Y when advancing the saved golfer coordinates.
High second cup coordinate saved at $29DE and read at $9354 during distance and bearing calculation.
Polygon index used to select the pointer-table entries and per-polygon vertex count. $218A advances it after finishing the current polygon's delta stream.
Saved first course-motion displacement byte. $2A98 keeps it after subtracting the previous component at $2A96.
Second course-motion displacement byte. $2A9E saves the result paired with $46 for later adjustment of the saved location.
Pixel value selected by the alternate polygon entries at $31F3 through $31FB. The writer at $2F19 shifts it into the active multicolour pair.
Projection status for the first edge endpoint, stored from A at $2D5D. The clipper reads it alongside the second endpoint status.
Projection status for the second edge endpoint from $2D83. The clipper's status checks use it to decide which endpoint needs adjustment.
First coordinate of the segment's current endpoint. $2E3F applies the primary-axis increment and $2E77 applies the extra step when needed.
Second coordinate of the rasterizer's current endpoint, updated at $2E48 and $2E80 as the segment advances.
First coordinate of the destination endpoint. $2DF5 reads it for the X-axis delta.
Second coordinate of the destination endpoint. The indexed subtraction at $2E0C computes the Y-axis distance using this byte on its first pass.
Polygon painter's working fill pattern. $32C7 loads it for the paint path selected by the row's partial-byte state.
$9313 stores the selected multicolour pixel pair mask. The polygon painter also rotates this working mask to address adjacent pairs.
The active pair's low bit mask set at $9318. $33ED ORs it into the modified bitmap byte.
Carries the replacement bits of a masked bitmap write. The common store at $BB03 combines them with the retained destination bits.
The mask at $9322 selects neighbouring pixels to preserve. $BB01 applies it before combining the replacement bits.
Working within-byte position. $9324 stores the selected multicolour pair number and the painter advances its copy at $3361.
X step held for the secondary axis when Y is the longer axis. $2E77 adds it after the accumulated error crosses the main delta.
Saved Y step for a Y-major segment. $2E46 adds this byte as part of the per-iteration Y advance.
Signed X increment prepared at $2DE7 and $2E05. $2E3F applies it before the error accumulator update.
Signed Y increment used by $2E7E when the error accumulator calls for an extra step.
High byte carried out of the error addition at $2E50. $2E70 propagates the borrow when the main delta is subtracted.
Low byte of the line error accumulator. $2E38 starts it at half the major-axis delta and $2E50 adds the minor delta each iteration.
Low workspace byte of the multiplication operand and result. $248E supplies it before the signed multiply in the coordinate transform.
Second product byte in the multiply workspace. $2497 rotates this byte first when doubling the signed product.
Third multiply workspace byte. $2499 shifts in the carry from the byte at $5C.
High workspace byte of the four-byte product. $249B rotates the carry into this byte before fixed-point rounding.
Low byte of the multiplication's second word. $2486 places the low rotation factor here for one component of the coordinate transform.
High byte paired with $5F. $248A places the high rotation factor here before calling the signed word multiplier.
Low byte of the divisor in the shift-and-subtract division at $9975. The trial remainder subtraction reads it at $998A.
High byte of the divisor. $9977 combines it with $61 to detect a zero divisor before trying the sixteen quotient bits.
Low byte of the dividend and resulting quotient workspace, shifted by $997F. The score display also loads this byte before decimal conversion.
High byte of the quotient workspace, receiving the low carry at $9981 while supplying the next bit to the remainder.
Low remainder workspace, shifted at $9983 and read for the trial subtraction at $9988.
High remainder workspace shifted at $9985 before the trial high-byte subtraction.
Low three Y bits saved at $2F39. $2F65 adds them to the computed bitmap cell base.
Pair position used to index the four-cell preserve masks at $2F2B before the pixel is merged into the destination.
Prepared pixel bits saved at $2F26 and combined with the preserved neighbouring bits at $2F30.
Whole character-cell row calculated by shifting the bitmap Y position right three times at $92F8–$92FA.
Saves the incoming pixel X at $92FD so the bitmap locator can select the pair number after finding the row address.
Source row offset into the shape mask. $AEA8 fetches that byte and $AEC8 advances the scan to its strip width.
Destination offset in the bitmap strip. $AED5 uses the low three bits to detect moving into a new eight-row cell.
The current mask bit tested by $AEAA before the corresponding terrain bitmap pixel is updated.
Saved top Y of the shape mask, computed at $AE68 by subtracting the two strip offsets from the projected centre plus one.
Starting bitmap X after left clipping. $AE56 keeps a positive start and $AE52 clamps a negative start to zero while putting its magnitude in $D9.
Low byte of the rounded fixed-point product stored by $24A0. The path at $24B0 can copy the input coordinate in directly.
High transformed coordinate byte paired with $73, held in Y on return from the rounding call at $249D.
Low rotation operand from $26DE. $2486 uses it as the low multiplier for the $D3/$D4 component.
High rotation operand paired with $75. $24A7 checks its sign before the alternate scaling path.
Low rotation operand supplied at $26CE and copied to the multiplier by $24BF.
High rotation operand supplied at $26D0 and copied to $60 at $24C3.
Low byte of the difference between the first coordinate and the saved player's position, stored by $270F.

Low byte of the difference between the second saved coordinate and the origin at $28F2, calculated by $271B.
High byte of the second coordinate offset, stored at $2726 with borrow from the low subtraction.
Range or special motion mode byte. The range selection sets it before choosing RNG and the range depth test at $38FB uses it as a gate.
Zero-based hole index. The scorecard renderer uses it as the inclusive final hole for partial rounds and tests against nine before drawing the back nine.
Left column of the screen and colour fill written at $139E. The row loop reloads this starting column at $13BD.
The stick poll combines active directions and fire with the caller's pending value.
Synthetic control bits selected by the demo stage machine. The gameplay controller uses them when the demo stage is active and there is no live input.
Current animation frame index used by the raster pose update.
Low first cup coordinate read into X at $9349. The saved copy is restored by $29CE before measuring the distance to the cup.
Low second cup coordinate, restored by $29D9 and read at $9352 when calculating the distance between the golfer and cup.
Incremented from the CIA swing timer while a swing timing phase is active.
Phase selector for the power and snap timer paths. Zero leaves the swing updates idle.
Zero-based player index chosen by the turn-order routine.

Projected polygon count loaded by $2D51 and $310F. The edge classifier decrements a copy to select the closing vertex.
Clip status belonging to the edge's first endpoint. $31A7 copies it into the appended vertex flags.
Clip status belonging to the edge's second endpoint. $31B9 copies it alongside the endpoint at $31B1 and $31B6.

Selects the bitmap font base through the tables at $5FD5 and $5FD9.
Starts at zero at $28FE and toggles at $0DCD. $3FEF tests it to select the table value or the value divided by four plus four.
The low byte of the indirect address, set at $2F0C to four times the immediate index at $2F06.

Byte reused as an indexed row column during glyph decoding and as the temporary subtraction term computed by $94E4 before launch arithmetic.

Low first input coordinate for the view transform. $22F3 stores the terrain coordinate plus the saved player offset before $24C5 reads it.

First untransformed coordinate low byte, saved from X after the divide by twelve at $22E7.
First untransformed coordinate high byte, saved from A at $22EC alongside the low result at $D5.

Count of pixels to skip when the projected shape extends past the left edge. $AE4E stores the magnitude of the negative start.
Secondary horizontal coordinate in the terrain mask drawing loop. $AF0B advances this value and $AF4F reloads it for positioning the bitmap pointer.
Shared display row or column counter. The sprite position conversion at $9289 saves it for restoring Y at $929D, while the panel advances its own cursor at $B780.

Bitmap scan limit used by the partial-row painter. $324C and $3255 compare against this limit before choosing the edge treatment.
Low first coordinate of the world-position triple. $3B92–$3B98 update it with the integrated displacement and carry into $E2.
Low second coordinate of the ball-position triple. $2C73 stores it from the position update and $3904 reads it for the range depth comparison.
Low third coordinate from the converted terrain position at $2DB9, paired with the high byte at $E4.

High third coordinate used along with $E1. $29C9 restores it from the active golfer's saved field and $2DBB installs a projected vertex's value.

High packed layout pointer byte, updated by $11F8 after advancing past the current row.
Terrain mask size index. $AE38 selects the horizontal size from the index and $AECA reloads it to stop on the selected strip width.

Terrain scan counter. The code at $ADEF increments it and $AE05 reloads it for the next object pass.
Full width selected for the current mask at $AE61. The horizontal pass compares its current position against this width at $AEF7.

Caption bitmap destination pointer high byte. $CF76 reloads it when advancing the destination to the next row.

Extension of the packed loader's accumulated offset. The offset loop increments it at $CECC on a carry into that byte.

High source pointer used by the bitmap glyph copy, calculated at $1249 with carry from the low-byte bank addition.

Active bitmap or matrix row. The full scorecard layout passes increment this byte after each decoded row and stop at twenty-five.
KERNAL keyboard queue. The restart path at $1DF3 injects a slash here after setting the buffered character count at $C6.
The keyboard wrapper at $12BA writes $40 after SCNKEY and GETIN and before returning to the game.
Low RAM IRQ vector byte written by $0E1D. The entry at $FF48 transfers through the indirect vector at this address.
High RAM IRQ vector byte. $0E22 sets it to $0E to join the low byte $39 from $0E1D.
Low byte of the indirect NMI vector. $14C2 installs $C1.
High byte of the indirect NMI vector. $14C7 installs $FE.
First rectangle's inclusive minimum X, indexed by object ID. Written at $B021 and tested at $B261 and $B2B4.
Second rectangle's inclusive minimum X, written by $B002. The central contact handler also tests this boundary at $B308.
Destination buffer base for the drive receive store at $CE03. The reader traverses data after its block index has been initialized by the receive wrapper.

First rectangle's exclusive maximum X, computed as projected X plus the clipped mask span at $B039.
First nibble lookup column indexed by the decoder at $CE26. The packed-stream decoder uses its selected value as a variable-width field selector.

Second packed decoder lookup column. The decode routine uses it when reconstructing the offset fields for a backreference.

Second rectangle's exclusive maximum X, stored at $B01A and also tested by the central contact handler at $B313.
Third packed decoder lookup column. This address begins the high-byte adjustments paired with the other reconstructed offset data.
The parallel high-byte column produced by the loop at $CE38. The bitstream decoder adds its reconstructed high bytes to the output pointer at $CED5.

Interior entry at index 98 of the second projected rectangle's exclusive X bound column at $0640. The table is written by $B01A. The separate BIT at $0EF6 skips an alternate LDX instruction and leaves X unchanged.
First rectangle's inclusive minimum Y, stored by $B026 and compared by both pixel tests.
Second rectangle's inclusive minimum Y, stored by $B007 before adding the mask strip width for its opposite edge.
First rectangle's exclusive maximum Y, formed by adding the selected mask strip width to the projected origin at $B02A.
Interior entry at index 34 of the first projected rectangle's exclusive Y bound column at $0880, written by $B02D. The separate BIT at $2ED3 skips an alternate LDX instruction and leaves X unchanged.
Second rectangle's exclusive maximum Y, formed from the projected origin and its strip width at $B00B.
Counts selections of each terrain object in the depth sort at $ADE0. The setup at $AD67 zeros the table.
Object IDs in the order the drawing pass selects them. $ADE9 stores the ID at the current output index $ED.

Projected horizontal coordinates read by the polygon edge loop at $3220. The parity correction at $350E searches these coordinates for a fixed X and shifts entries for a missing endpoint.
Projected vertical coordinates paired with $0C40. The parity correction compares the matching Y entries and may insert Y 199 at $356B.
Per-vertex flags read by $323F when deciding whether to plot an endpoint. The correction at $3516 masks these flags before counting candidate vertices.
The row decoder at $1158 writes glyph indices here. The course panel draws from columns 30–39 and the setup panel layout code at $B807 also uses this buffer.
Set by fire at $15C1 and cleared after pose $1F by the animation routine.
Zero is cleared by the contact reset. The transition at $B726 changes phase one to two before starting putt motion.
Set by $160F on the first snap fire press.
Set when the fire release is captured for this stroke.
Result byte from the fixed bitmap pixel sampler at $B718. $3863 reads it to choose the launch adjustment path.
Stores the timing-derived snap index used by the launch and in-flight calculations.
Current club selection. The full shot path cycles across thirteen indices with the stick.
Timing-derived power value latched by the release handler and used by the launch calculation.
$1852 masks the low CIA1 timer byte to three bits before storing this variation input.
$1849 samples the high CIA1 timer A byte here for shot variation.
Zero-based round selector. The round caption draws this byte plus one and the score accumulator uses it to select the current round's result slots.
Cleared for the automatic setup at $A1D7 and at the one-player path at $A242.
$A3C9 compares the player's saved order against this rank, then $A3CE advances it when choosing an eligible golfer.
Four per-player flags. The per-hole reset clears them and $A34C marks the active player's first stroke.
Four per-player scale selectors, initialized to two at $A2CC. $29EA copies the current value from $88, and the shot logic compares the saved value with two.
Low bytes of the per-player distance values. The pre-stroke setup seeds them from $937D and the next golfer selector compares them after the high bytes.
High bytes of the per-player distance values initialized from $937E at $A369. $A3EB compares them first when selecting the golfer.
Alternate course line flag. $3E74 blocks the overhead view when this is set, and $A80E branches to the alternate line offsets.
Four player club selections updated at $1608 and restored for the active golfer at $1A1F. The initialization at $A2C4 sets them to zero.
Initial polygon index stored by $2ED6 and incremented at $2EFA after drawing the selected boundary.
The pose update at $0EA7 returns early when this byte is nonzero. Startup sets it to zero at $1558.
The contact path combines this mask with $0D54 at $35B4 while choosing the ball and marker sprite enable bits.
The motion stop path sets a flag here and the shot initializer clears it in the contact reset.
Cleared by $B64A, updated when the ball contacts an object and tested at $B16C before changing the collision response.
Second pair of shadow-pixel object bounds result bits. The write at $B2FE feeds the combined contact test at $B0C8.
First pair of shadow-pixel object bounds result bits, set at $B2D6 and ORed with the other bounds results at $B0C5.
A nonzero joystick sample sets this byte at $12E7 after clearing the demo phase.
Timer slot fifteen's raster path increments this counter at $0E88.
Decremented at $0E8B alongside the increment of $0D30 in the slot fifteen raster path.
Result of the second ball-pixel bounds check in the group. $B2AB writes the chosen zero or one.
Result of the first ball-pixel bounds check in the group, written at $B283 and tested with the other object bounds results.
Initialized to one at $B04F. The path following a zero first projection status clears it and calls the ball pixel classifier.
The sprite 6 classifier stores the sampled pair at $B19C and can replace it with five at $B1F3. The combined test at $B05F uses its low bit.
$37D3 clears this byte when launching a putt, and the general motion setup also clears it at $2BB4.
Used by $3951 and $395F while scaling the two horizontal velocity components after contact. Putt launch initializes it to $80.
The velocity update subtracts this byte at $39AC, and the motion initialization writes it at $2BF5.
Gate checked at $3B18 before integrating coordinates. $37F7 enables it for putt motion.
$3829 supplies the magnitude of the lateral correction added at $3A12 or subtracted at $3A24 depending on the meter result.
$0EBE compares the desired pose with this cached index. A change updates it before refreshing sprite pointers and positions.
The ball sprite classifier saves its converted Y here at $B196. The strip test uses it for the interval comparison after matching X.
The ball sprite classifier saves its converted X at $B193. The strip test compares it with the strip's fixed coordinate before testing Y.
$35A2 saves the low depth reference. $3906 compares the ball's current low depth with it when the high depth byte is zero.
Sprite 7's sampler stores the initial value at $B205 and the classifier may replace it at $B258. $B05F combines it with the ball contact code at $0D37.
The shadow sprite classifier saves its converted Y here before reading the pixel at $B202.
Integer part of the integrated step for the current axis. $3B8B increments it on remainder accumulation overflow before applying it to the position.
First element of the three-byte per-axis motion remainder array indexed by X at $3B79.
Second motion remainder byte. The startup at $1563 initializes it before the per-axis loop begins using the array.
Last byte of the motion remainder array $0D46,X. The integration loop begins with this slot at X=2.
Low component saved from X at $3C27. The landing response reads it at $3974 before scaling.
Low component written at $3C3A and retrieved in X by the landing response at $398D.
$3A79 saves the projected X. $3A9D adds the screen-to-sprite offset before writing both sprite X registers.
$3A7C saves projected ball Y and $3A96 replaces it with Y plus $32 for sprite 6.
$3FFA saves projected shadow Y, used at $3AC7 before adding the sprite offset for sprite 7.
Sprite enable mask initialized with bits six and seven at $1A61. Display and contact paths alter the bits as the sprites are drawn or hidden.
The integrator loads this byte as a positive divisor at $3B4F. Setup initializes it to fifty.
$1A3F clears this byte before the shot loop. $1AEF checks it before marking the range ball and displaying its distance.
The shadow sprite classifier saves the converted X at $B1FC. The projected strip test matches this coordinate before testing the interval in Y.
Starts at $C0 at $B03F. Object contact paths clear selected bits and $35B1 combines this mask with the sprite flags.
Loop bound loaded from the selected polygon vertex count at $2D4C. $2D72 wraps to vertex zero on reaching this limit.

Set at $AE3E from half the selected shape width and subtracted from the projected mask centre to locate the left edge.

High byte of the lateral aim coordinate, paired with zero-page $3F.
High component paired with $83. $29D3 restores it with the other saved cup coordinates before measuring distance and bearing.

High first coordinate copied from $E2. Subtraction at $3E13 uses it with the borrow from the paired low coordinate.
High camera depth copied from $E3 and paired with $0D6C for perspective projection.
High third coordinate staged from $E4. $3E3E loads it as the high dividend for the second overhead projection.

Initialized to two at $157F alongside the initial distance display scale at $88.
$3C2C stores the high component paired with $0D49. The landing path reloads it into Y at $3977.
$3C3F stores the high component paired with $0D4A. $3990 reloads it for the landing adjustment.
The putt launch sets this byte to two at $37D8. The general motion setup also updates it at $2BB9.

Cleared at $19B2 after deriving the last polygon index and before choosing the first golfer.

$9495 saves the current Y endpoint before the projected strip bound updates.
Set by the range selection at $A217. The shot loop tests it to bypass normal cup distance display and the disc dispatch uses it for RNG.

Nonzero makes $2A59 return without drawing its reference glyphs. $2932 clears it in the new golfer-position path.

$1C96 clears it alongside the pose and putting animation flag during putting sprite setup.
$199A writes it during the state setup before the first golfer is chosen.
The shot loop clears it at $1A17 and checks it at $1AFA after displaying the range result. The collision path updates it at $B41B.
Cleared when starting a projected outline. The edge entry at $3228 sets it before jumping to the rasterizer.
Working state set by the clipper at $3014. The boundary pass reads it at $3164 after updating its saved copy.
$2AC4 records this adjustment and $29AE adds it to the active golfer's saved high view coordinate.

Sign classification of the vertical difference from the last projected vertex to the first. $3433 stores $FF, 0 or 1.
Signed direction of the edge from the current vertex to its target. $3456 stores the comparison result for the fill logic.

Selects escape byte $FF and the glyph buffer as destination, then joins the common row runs decoder.

Immediate compare operand patched at $11B9 from the decoder entry's choice of $44 or $FF.

Adds eight to $FD/$FE with carry into the high byte and preserves A.
Multiplies the column in A by eight and adds it to the bitmap row pointer at $FD/$FE, propagating both carries into the high byte.
Uses the row index in X to load the low and high bitmap address bytes into $FD/$FE from the tables at $1488 and $14A1.
Banks in the KERNAL, enables keyboard row outputs, then calls SCNKEY and GETIN. Returns the resulting PETSCII byte in A after restoring port $35. A nonzero byte also goes to $AD32.
Operand of the LDA at $12A4. The value $36 exposes the KERNAL for SCNKEY and GETIN. The caller restores $35 before returning the key.

Saves both CIA1 data directions and makes both ports inputs. Reads port 2 through $DC00, inverts the active-low signals and ORs the five control bits into $80 when there is input. Restores both direction registers before returning.
Copies CIA1 data direction registers to $FB and $FC for the stick poll.
Writes $FC and $FB back to CIA1 port B and A directions and reads back both ports.
Clears bit 0 of CIA1 control register A, preserving the other bits.
Sets bits 0 and 3 of CIA1 control register A to start timer A in one-shot mode.
Copies eight bytes from the source at ($FB) to the bitmap destination at ($FD). The usual entry sets Y to 7.
Uses A as a mask of sprite positions whose X high bits should be cleared in $D010. Restores A.
ORs A into the VIC sprite enable register and restores A.
Clears the bits of the sprite enable register $D015 selected by the mask in A. Preserves A.
Uses A as a mask of sprite bits to clear in $D01D, then restores A.
Clears the selected sprite height-doubling bits in $D017 and returns the original mask in A.
Clears the mask's selected bits in the sprite multicolour register $D01C, preserving A.
Stores the event byte in both $0D98,X and $0DB9,X and sets the active flag at $0DA9,X to one.
Calls the width and height expansion clear routines with the same A mask. Each helper preserves A.
Clears the priority bits selected by A in $D01B so those sprites are drawn in front of the bitmap. Restores A.
Fills colour RAM with A and the screen colour matrix with Y. X indexes four tables that supply the first and stopping rows and the first and stopping columns.
Low indexed colour store operand. The row setup installs it at $13AB and the loop adds forty as each row ends.
High indexed colour store operand written by $13B4. A carry from adding forty to the low operand advances this byte.
Low indexed screen matrix store operand. $13AE gives it the same low byte as the colour store's initial address.
High indexed screen store operand selected by $13BA for the current row and incremented at $13D9 on page crossing.
Operand of the compare at $13C9. The row fills thirty cells, advances the patched matrix and colour RAM store addresses forty bytes and repeats until row 25.
Immediate comparison endpoint for the rectangle row loop. The branch at $13E8 repeats until the endpoint is reached.
The first screen row for each of the eleven fill rectangles selected by X at $138E.
Exclusive stop row for each preset passed to the screen and colour fill.
Inclusive start column for each preset rectangle in $138E.
Exclusive column bound written to the immediate operand at $13CA.
Adds $18 to A, returns zero if the result is negative and limits nonnegative values to $30.
Reads every address in the $FE and $FF pages with the KERNAL visible and writes the bytes back into underlying RAM.
Low byte of row times 40, shared by the screen matrix and the colour RAM row addresses.
High bytes of the 25 colour RAM row starts at $D800 plus 40 times the row.
High bytes of the 25 matrix row starts at $6000 plus 40 times the row.
Low bytes of the 25 bitmap row starts at $4000 plus 320 times the character row.
High byte of each bitmap character row address. The pixel address setup at $2F36 combines it with $1488, a horizontal offset and the in-cell row.
Sets the NMI vector and CIA directions, copies the interrupt pages, selects VIC bank $4000 and multicolour bitmap mode, clears audio and initializes the default names and skills.
Clears per-round working state, configures the timer and resets the current player and hole indices before jumping to the load sequence at $1946.
Saves $39 and $0D0B across clearance of the game RAM and zero-page work areas.
Zeros $39–$70, $D1–$F2 and $73–$8F, including shot and temporary coordinates.
Clears the pending stick bits and polls port 2. If fire is held, sets the swing animation flag at $0D00.
Changes the club index on up or down and wraps it through 0–12. Redraws the club indication, arms a repeat delay and stores the club for the active player.
If the snap flag is clear, samples the stick and latches the first fire press. Stores the low nibble of timing byte $85 at $0D05 below $2F, or $0E from $2F onward.
When the flag at $0D02 is zero, sets $0D05 to fourteen and marks $0D02 as one.
Sets the CPU port directions to $2F and resets output bit three. The forced zero at $1658 makes the branch at $165A skip the store to $97B5.
While the release flag is clear, waits for the fire bit to clear. Latches the release and converts timing byte $85 to the power value at $0D07, with different rules before and after $10.
When $0D03 is zero, clears the captured power byte and sets $0D03 to one.
Refills four eight-byte meter positions with $AA, restores the marker bytes and clears the ball-in-motion and swing input flags.
Steps the pose index when the animation timer expires. Uses a per-pose delay table, calls phase handlers at selected indices and clears the swing flag at index $20.
Thirty-two render tick durations, indexed by pose and passed to the animation timer.
Stops CIA1 timer A, reloads $FFFF, starts one-shot mode and resets the swing phase while interrupts are masked.
Under IRQ masking, stops the CIA timer, sets its latch to $A800 and clears the meter position $85. Restarts the timer and records phase 1 at $86.
Under IRQ masking, loads the CIA timer with $2300 and sets the meter position to $10. Restarts the timer and sets phase 2 at $86.
Under IRQ masking, loads the CIA timer with $1A00 and sets the meter position to $20. Restarts the timer and sets phase 3 at $86.
Masks IRQs, stops the timer and calls $175A if the recorded phase was three. Re-enables IRQs before returning.
Disables sprites 0–5, loads their starting coordinate pairs and pointers, sets their colours, and resets the pose and previously drawn pose to zero.
Six interleaved X/Y pairs copied into VIC registers $D000–$D00B by $17F4.
Six sprite colour bytes copied to $D027–$D02C by the loop at $1801.
Four colours indexed by active golfer and written to the colour register for sprite 2 at $1817.
Saves the timer A high byte and the low three bits of the low byte at $0D09/$0D08, then calls $0E03 with $26.
Uses twice the club index to read a two-glyph code from the table at $1881 and draws it at row $11, column $26.
Start of the first-glyph column indexed by the club caption renderer at $1872.
Second byte of each of thirteen two-glyph club captions. The lookup at $187A uses twice the club index. The first glyph column begins one byte earlier at $1881.
Selects glyph bank 1 and calls the cup distance and bearing calculation before falling into the shot-yardage renderer.

Ones digit produced by the decimal loop at $18D2 and updated with the mode's ones adjustment.

Three adjustment values for the tens position, added at $18F8 and reduced by ten when needed.
Three offsets applied to the high yardage digit at $1907 after the low two digits have been adjusted.

Loads the TF file selected for the course, copies its staged data into RAM beneath I/O and loads the hole file. Offers retry on disk errors. After a successful load it reads par at $C557 and transfers control to the hole loop.
Increments the zero-based hole index and reloads while the result is below 18. At 18 it offers the print path, checks the round limit and either resets the hole index for the next round or restarts.
XORs each of ten bytes from $1A05 with $FF and writes the result at $FF58–$FF61. This supplies the RAM interrupt dispatch while the KERNAL is hidden.
Bytewise complements of the ten-byte interrupt stub installed at $FF58.
Selects the active player's club from $0D1F, initialises shot and golfer display state, then polls aim and shot input while awaiting a stroke.
Calls $1B87. If a demonstration is running, advances its step and shot index and releases synthetic joystick input. Restores the sound filter configuration.
When $0D7D is set, computes distance from the $1800,$0500 reference, divides by 36 and updates the displayed yardage with glyph bank 1.
In range mode, checks whether sprite 6 is enabled. Converts its position to bitmap coordinates, selects pixel mode two and calls $2F16.
Selects the $21 argument for timer slot zero. The overlapping BITs skip the shorter arguments before the timer request at $1B94.
Supplies transition selector $1B. Two BIT instructions skip the selectors at the overlapping entries $1B8D and $1B90. Calls $1370 with X zero and waits for $0DA9 to clear.
Clears the accumulated stick bits, handles slash restart and samples the stick until the active-high fire bit is set. Queues timer slot zero with $1B, then waits for its active byte to clear.
Tests the mask in A against $80 and returns to the wait at $1BA1 when it is clear. Once set, passes $1B to $1370 and waits until $0DA9 clears.
Calls the slash restart handler during the joystick wait loop and returns to sample the stick.
Calls $1CE5 and fills the first 240 bitmap bytes of each character row from 5 through 24 with alternating $CC and $33.
Advances the putting pose when the raster timer expires, sets the four changing sprite pointers, and calls the launch routine at pose 6. Clears the active flag at pose 10.
Ten animation delays indexed by the putting pose at $1C11. The selected delay is passed to timer slot zero at $1C16.
Loads five pages of the putting animation from frame packet 16. Sets the sprite pointers, positions, colours and initial putting state.
Five starting colours for sprites 0 through 4. The loop at $1C7F applies them before the player accent overrides sprite 0.
Ten sprite pointers for putting sprite 0 indexed by pose at $1BF9. The initializer uses the first value at $1C5F.
Ten pose-dependent sprite pointers for VIC sprite 1, selected at $1BFF and loaded to $63F9.
Ten indices into the VIC sprite bank for sprite 2. The putting pose update copies the selected byte into $63FA.
Fixed sprite 3 pointer read by the putting initializer and installed at $63FB by $1C74.
Ten indices for the fifth putting sprite. The pose update at $1C0B uses the current pose and the initialization at $1C77 uses pose 0.
Sets the play text bank and draws 25 rows of the bitmap layout, colour layer and third template layer in separate passes.
Waits for the raster boundary, fills the indicated play rectangle and conditionally applies two status colour overrides based on $0D81. Sets VIC background colour 9.
Fills the playfield pattern through $1BBE, redraws panel rows through $B83D, then sets the course background colours. Restores CPU port directions to $2F.
Draws the putting controls and golfer, polls aim and fire until the stroke starts, then updates ball projection, ground drag and sound until the putt and its animation finish.
Checks ball height, distance from the reference point and bitmap pixels below the ball. Decrements the ground movement multiplier up to four times when the ball requires the drag adjustment.
Restores the eight-by-eight meter glyph bytes and the eight initial timing marker bytes in the bitmap.
Enters only while fire is pressed. Draws the initial eight putt meter positions, then times the remaining fire hold in two-tick intervals and remembers the level when fire is released.
Operand of the comparison at $1F4B. A release in bucket nine sets $0D77. The marked path fills the selected strip when the bucket is at least eight.
Uses the power bucket in X to select one bitmap strip from $5778 through $5EF8. Writes the fill pattern in A to the byte offset in Y.
Builds the right-side bitmap panel, sets up its colours and writes successive strips of glyphs from the panel table.
Two 48-byte groups of source pixel pairs used by the green marker overlay.
Enters the shared cursor setup with X=0. The BIT instructions skip the alternate immediate loads.
Alternate LDX entry inside the operand of the BIT at $20AC. Selects X=1 before skipping the next entry.
Reads a per-group count and paired start coordinates from the hole data. Expands signed X and Y deltas into split low and high coordinate lists with a separate destination for each shape group.
Low destination address byte patched from $BB4A by $2107. The store at $214D writes the cumulative X low byte.
The high operand of the indexed store at $214D. Patched from $BB4B by $210D. The next instructions add the signed delta's high byte with the carry from its low byte.
Low destination address byte installed at $2113. The store at $2159 writes the cumulative X high byte after signed carry propagation.
High byte of the indexed X high-byte store at $2159. The setup reads the destination from $BB5A/$BB5B and patches it at $2116–$2119 before decoding vertices.
Low destination address byte selected by $211F from the boundary Y-low pointers.
High byte of the destination operand at $2170. $2125 installs the high byte from the polygon's pointer at $BB6B.
Low destination address byte installed at $212B for the cumulative Y high-byte store.

High operand byte of the indexed store at $217C. The polygon setup copies it from the selected pointer at $BB7B,X. The loop advances through vertex pairs and then either begins the next polygon or dispatches the final coordinate pair at $219F.
Number of polygons selected in the hole header. The delta decoder stops when the next polygon index reaches this value.
Low origin byte read by $21B5 before applying the first signed X delta.
High origin byte loaded alongside $21A5 when initializing the polygon X accumulator.
Low origin byte copied from the hole descriptor at $20D7 and used to initialize the Y accumulator.
High Y origin byte read from the hole descriptor at $20DB. $21CA copies it into the initial Y delta accumulator.
Starting cursor in the coordinate stream. The parser first zeros it and reloads Y here before beginning the signed-pair loop.
Limit read from offset zero of the polygon stream. The decoder checks X against it after emitting each coordinate pair.
$2147 adds the decoded X delta to this low byte and $214D emits the updated result.
Cumulative X high byte. The add at $2153 includes carry from the low result and the delta's sign extension.
$216A adds the next Y delta and stores the new low component here.
Cumulative high Y with sign and carry adjustment from the paired low byte. $217C emits it into the polygon column.
Set to zero or $FF by the polygon reader and included in the accumulator high-byte addition. The projection routine at $3D42 also uses the address as temporary workspace.
Restores both 16-bit cumulative boundary coordinates from $21A5–$21A8 to $21AF–$21B2 before decoding the next polygon.
Puts the decoded hole record address $C554 in $FB–$FC.
Returns the pair X:Y pointing to $C558 in the decoded hole header.
Returns the pair X:Y pointing to $C559 in the decoded hole header.
Returns the hole header pointer $C557 in X and Y.
Calls $220C for an index in $FB/$FC, doubles it and adds $C59D to produce the address of the corresponding two-byte entry.
Adds the index from $220C to $C55D and stores the resulting address in $FD/$FE.
Computes a byte offset of sixteen times $0D7B plus twice $45 and returns it in $FB–$FC.

Computes the cup position relative to the decoded hole origin and stores both coordinate words at $2A21–$2A24. Calls the view transform unless $0D97 is set.
Returns the low byte in X and high byte in A. If $C55B is nonnegative, adds it to the word at $21A5. Otherwise subtracts its ones' complement. The caller then scales the result through $2DBE.

Walks each decoded boundary group, shifts coordinates relative to the player and applies the current golf projection unless overhead mode is selected. Writes transformed vertices back to the working column arrays.
Walks the terrain record columns backwards, rotates their points into the player view unless overhead mode is set and applies the lower depth bound before storing them.

Derives rotation coefficients from A and Y, combines the cup coordinates at $2A21 with the view offsets at $79 through $7C, then rotates that point. Stores the transformed coordinates at $83/$0D65 and $84/$44, rebasing X by $1800.
Takes the polygon number in A and loads four two-byte column addresses from the interleaved pointer tables at $BB4A, $BB5A, $BB6A and $BB7A.
Copies four bytes from zero page $F3–$F6 to scratch memory at $246F–$2472.
Four-byte staging area for $F3–$F6, written by $2468 and read by $2476 before the original pointers are restored.
Copies back the saved pointer bytes from $246F–$2472 to $F3–$F6.
Forms the two components of a coordinate transform from inputs at $D1–$D4 and coefficients at $75–$78. Multiplies and rescales each term before subtracting into $D5–$D6 and adding into $D7–$D8.
Reflects the phase in A:Y into the first quadrant, fetches neighbouring 16-bit table entries and interpolates using the low phase byte. Negates the result for the negative half-cycle.
Quarter-wave endpoint flag. The interpolation starts it at zero and $258A sets $FF at the exact table endpoint for the return in X.
Quadrant sign flag saved at $257F or $25B5. $260D selects whether to negate the interpolated value.
Low angle byte for the quarter-wave interpolation. $25EA loads it as the fractional multiplier between adjacent table entries.
High angle byte adjusted for the selected quadrant. Its doubled value selects a cosine word in the quarter-wave table.
Low byte of the uninterpolated table value saved at $25D3. The interpolator subtracts the scaled difference and returns the result in Y.
High byte of the selected table word, stored at $25D6 and adjusted with borrow from the low-byte interpolation at $2608.
Saves the incoming angle from A:Y, subtracts $4000, and passes the adjusted angle in A:Y to the quarter-wave lookup at $2566.
Sixty-four little-endian values approaching zero from $7FFF. The quarter-wave routine and its inverse angle search use adjacent entries for interpolation.
Alias one byte into the little-endian cosine table. Indexed with an even offset to read the high byte of the current cosine value.
Alias for the next entry's low byte with the current entry's even index. $287D reads it to form the interpolation denominator.
Alias for the high byte of the next cosine entry. Together with $2645, lets the interpolator read neighbouring words without advancing X.
Final zero word of the cosine table at a quarter turn. The table starts at $2643 with $7FFF.
Saves the angle in A and Y, interpolates two quarter-wave coefficients, then stores the coefficient words and the quadrant adjustment flags used by $247F.
Low view angle held by $26C5 while the first coefficient is calculated. $26D5 retrieves it into Y for the other coefficient.
High view angle saved from A at $26C8 and restored at $26D8 for the second coefficient.
Sign mode saved at $26E2. The coordinate transform uses its high bit to choose the normal multiplication or alternate scaling at $247F.
Sign mode stored by $26D2 after the other coefficient lookup, tested at $24B8 before multiplying the first coordinate input.
Uses the active golfer's stored angle to resolve a vector of length $0500, then subtracts the golfer's coordinates from the resulting view anchor and records two offsets at $79–$7C.
Computes squared distance between two course points, adding the squares of the signed X and Z separations into $28F4–$28F7.
Writes $2F into the processor direction register at $00 and returns with the mask in A.

Uses successive averages of a trial value and squared distance divided by that value. When the trial stops decreasing, adds the discarded half bit and returns that estimate in X and Y. Inputs zero and one take the A-return path.
Compares four bytes at $63–$66 against $28F8–$28FB from the highest byte down. Returns the flags from the deciding comparison when the words differ.
Uses the coordinate delta and distance to form a scaled ratio, searches the quarter-wave table and interpolates the angle between adjacent entries.
Saves the interpolated fraction in $43, reflects the angle across $4000, and uses the signs of the two course deltas to adjust it to the correct quadrant. Sets $0D81 when done.
Low difference of the second planar coordinate, stored at $275E before squaring it for the cup distance.
High difference paired with $28F2. The bearing routine uses its sign to select a quadrant.
Lowest byte of the squared distance. First receives the low first-axis square and then the low sum of both squares.
Second squared-distance byte. $277D adds the matching second-axis square byte with the low carry.
Third byte of the accumulated squares, updated from the third multiplication result at $2788.
Highest byte of the squared-distance sum. $2793 propagates carry from the three lower byte additions.
Low copy of the squared distance. The integer-distance routine uses the copy during its running comparison and partial result calculation.
Second byte of the squared-distance working copy, synchronized by the store at $2783 after the sum.
Third byte of the working copy of both squared coordinate differences. $278E stores this byte before the distance routine changes the copy.
Top byte of the squared-distance working copy, written at $2799 from the high addition before the square-root pass.

Clears putting state and VIC sprite enables, sets default coordinates and builds the opening view for a golfer who has yet to play. Takes the saved-state path at $293B when that player's flag in $2A1D is set.
Four bytes of the first saved golfer-position component, restored into $DF for the active golfer at $29BA.

Uses $2729 to subtract the point in $DF/$E2 and $E1/$E4 from the anchor $1800,$0500. Negates the resulting signed components. Saves integer distance at $2AC9–$2ACA and the derived angle at $2AC8 and $0D89.

Converts the selected polygon group into projected edges at successively higher trial heights. When a clipped case is flagged, reruns the edge builder at reference height and fills the resulting visible span.
Vertical spacing for the raised terrain layers. The routine initializes it to three and increases it with the projected minimum depth before drawing.

Steps from the two endpoint coordinates along the dominant axis, using the distance accumulator to step the other axis. Hands each pixel inside the 120-by-200 course area to the selected segment painter.

Sets $0D8A to one and walks the polygons from the last index down to zero. Calls $2C56 for each polygon.

Selects X=0 and uses an overlapping BIT at $2ED3 to skip the alternate immediate load before storing the index at $2ED6.

Loads the patchable index at $2F06 and derives four times that value for both Y and the pointer low byte used by the indirect store.

Given bitmap pixel coordinates in X and Y, selects its row base, cell and scanline. Patches both operands used by the pixel plotting routine and saves the two-bit pixel index.
Four masks that clear a single two-bit field and preserve the other three. Indexed by the pixel's within-byte pair number.
Rejects a line whose endpoint masks share an outside bit. Swaps endpoints when the first alone is outside, then clips the second against X 0 or 239 or Y 0 or 199 as indicated.
Low byte of the jump target at $2FA8. The adjacent paths intersect the line against Y zero or the X edges and repeat the visibility test at $2F7D.

Exchanges the endpoints, high coordinates, outcodes and clipping work fields. Records the swap at $0D88.
Takes edge Y in A and intersects the segment from $4B/$4C to $4D/$4E using the signed X delta divided by the Y delta. Replaces the second endpoint and sets $4A for X below 0 or at least 240.
Takes edge X in A and intersects the segment using the signed Y delta divided by the X delta. Replaces the second endpoint at $4D/$4E and sets $4A for Y below 0 or at least 200.
Clears bit 3 at $01 with mask $F7, then returns the masked value in A. This bit is the cassette write line.
Copies the 32-bit product from $5B–$5E to $63–$66 and divides it by the signed X difference from $30F7.
Copies the 32-bit product to the division workspace and divides it by the signed Y difference from $30E9.
Subtracts the first endpoint word from the second using low bytes $4C and $4E and high bytes $2FCF and $2FD1. Returns the signed difference in Y:X.
Subtracts the X word at $2FCE:$4B from $2FD0:$4D and returns the difference in Y:X.

Projects successive polygon vertices, wraps the endpoint index to zero, clips the edge and appends the resulting endpoint records to the projected vertex columns. Its caller closes and draws the resulting boundary.
Calls the edge-record insertion routine, advances the record count and returns to the edge loop.
Writes X, Y and endpoint flags from $4B, $4C and $8A into the projected vertex columns at index $89.
Writes X, Y and endpoint flags from $4D, $4E and $8B into the same columns at index $89.
Selects outline mode 2 in $48 before falling through to the closed projected outline path.

Loads line mode 1, then executes two BIT instructions over the immediate loads of the mode 2 and mode 3 entry points. Continues at $31FB with A unchanged.

Loads line mode 3 and falls into the common edge loop at $31FB. The loop reads pairs of projected X and Y vertices, connects adjacent vertices and wraps from the last vertex back to the first.
Loads the selected projected X and Y coordinates from the separate columns and returns them in X and A, respectively. Y remains the vertex index.
Sets the polygon edge flag at $0D87 and jumps to the line rasterizer after the clipping entry.

Rejects segments by their group flags and current pass, then paints along a projected bitmap row. The paths for type 2, type 3 and other types use different fill masks and tests against the existing pixels.

Forms X=$F7 from the immediate operands, masks the byte at $FF0A+X with $F7 and writes it back. The effective address is $0001 after 16-bit wrap.
Compares the current, previous and next vertex rows. Uses the relative X direction and neighbouring row signs to choose edge treatment flags at $0C80.
Checks the left and right screen limits for an odd count of selected edge flags. Inserts a bottom edge marker when needed so the later fill has a paired boundary.

Initialized to one for the closing pass and added by $352E while marking the candidate under consideration.

Vertex index saved at $3531 and compared with the later scan index at $3541 and $355F.

Zeros four flags at $0D87 and $0D8E–$0D90, copies $E0 into $0D42, resets CPU port directions to $2F and returns $26 in A.
Returns A=$26 after the processor direction write at $35A7. At $1B8F a BIT operand also uses this address to skip an alternate immediate.

Three consecutive nine-glyph captions. $35DA–$35E8 multiply the display scale index at $88 by nine and patch the traversal endpoint to nine entries beyond that start.

Clears the three sprite pages at $6400–$66FF and draws the small marker shapes. Sets sprite 6 coordinates and the initial aim coordinate to $1800, then calls the aim updater, which can leave sprite 7 coordinates unchanged when its latch is set.
Immediate operand of the sprite mask load at $3638. The conditional patch near $98F4 can write this byte.

Checks shot state and the update latch, then reads the stick. Left and right subtract or add one to the 16-bit aim coordinate at $0D64:$3F, with bounds depending on skill and play state. Projects the aim and updates sprite 7 coordinates.
Sets up putt parameters, collects the starting screen position, then sets $0D3C and $7D to enable coordinate integration and shot processing.
Uses the shot meter index in X to select a repeat count and adds the club-indexed value at $3844 that many times. Index 7 or a zero player flag selects zero. Stores the result at $0D3D.
Fifteen repeat counts indexed by the snap position. Count zero is the neutral entry at index 7.
Club-indexed increments used when turning the snap index into a movement component.
Stores 8 in the two meter fields at $0D9E and $0DBF and enables their update flag at $0DAF.
Combines club-indexed values with the shot parameters, calls the multiplication routine, then saves the products in the split velocity fields $3E:$E7 and $3D:$E6.
Thirteen per-club bytes. $387C subtracts the adjustment at $AE, adds the captured swing power and passes the byte to $9A4A for scaling.
Thirteen per-club factors applied by the multiply called from $3899. The high result bytes become $E7 and $3E.
Thirteen per-club factors read at $3FEC. The putting option selects the unmodified factor or the factor shifted right twice and increased by four.
Returns immediately when $7D is zero. Otherwise, if the high coordinate byte at $E3 is zero, compares $E0 with the cached reference at $0D42 and transfers to $BECA.
Tail-calls the flight acceleration routine when the range depth comparison sees a nonzero high coordinate byte at $E3.
Handles vertical contact with the reference height, scales velocities at impact and updates ground movement while the relevant timer is idle.
Copies ball sprite Y to shadow sprite Y and clears the shot-in-progress flag when all three velocities are zero.
Copies the two horizontal velocity words to their landing work fields before clearing the vertical velocity.
Advances lateral velocity according to snap index when vertical velocity is nonzero, applies the stored wind components off the reference height, and decreases vertical velocity by $26 on its timer.
Projects the ball and its reference-height position. Updates sprite 6 and 7 X, sets their high X bits from the screen offset carry and writes separate Y coordinates when the ball is off the tee.

When $0D3C is set, divides each signed velocity by the update divisor at $0D50. Carries the leftover fraction forward in $0D46,X and adds or subtracts the whole increment from the corresponding ball coordinate. Preserves the interrupted routine's arithmetic workspace.
Derives distance and projected offsets from aim and reference coordinates, then scales the shot velocity into two horizontal components saved for the landing update.
High operand of the store at $3C4B. The instruction at $3C50 writes $40 back to it.
Multiplies signed X/Y by the word in $D1/$D2 and divides the four-byte product by the word at $28F4. Returns the quotient low word in X/Y.
Checks motion and the height bound, then compares depth and lateral offsets with the cup location. Selects a capture threshold from the lateral difference.
Immediate operand of the first club-index comparison, patched together with $3CDA by $926F when the putting option is applied.
Immediate operand of CPX at $3CD9, patched at $9272 to 3 or 6 by the putt option. A match selects the low thresholds initialized at $3CDD. The following tests can raise the threshold to $E0.

Checks the putt speed, reference height and position fraction. If within the capture thresholds it hides the ball sprites and stops integration. Otherwise the response depends on the terrain and player skill fields.
Negates the two-byte lateral deflection when the saved cup-side flag is negative.
Low ball velocity bound for the cup test. $3D00 rejects values at or above the selected bound.
Low deflection component. The shift at $3D62 and $3D68 takes bits from its high byte before applying the chosen sign.
Sign selector for the putt deflection. A negative value makes $3D90 negate the low and high deflection components.
Scratch copy of A saved at $94AA when preparing one of the projected contact bounds.
Scratch copy of the Y coordinate saved at $94AF alongside the projected endpoint.
Pixel extraction scratch. $92A6 stores the masked pair during the shift loop, which moves the selected multicolour value toward the low bits of A.
Converts course coordinates to the overhead screen position with divisors $30 and $80. Returns the result around the horizontal and vertical reference points in X and Y.
On T, if its state check allows, disables sprites and switches projection, redraws hole geometry and terrain, and waits for another T. Re-enters the normal hole setup on return.
Fills the 30-cell-wide course area over 25 rows with alternating $CC and $33 bitmap bytes.
Clears the marker sprite page, builds the shapes and configures the sprites. Sprite 0 uses the active golfer's saved coordinates. Sprites 1 and 2 share the position projected from $2A21–$2A24.
When $5139 is $77, writes $FF into 80 consecutive bytes in four bitmap character rows starting at $5130, $5270, $53B0 and $54F0.
Sets the panel font, draws the 36-glyph row from $BE92 and clears input while switching the display into setup.
Reads the per-club value from $38EE with X. When $8F is set, divides that byte by four and adds four before returning it.
Clears interrupt disable and saves Y in $0D4D before returning.
Four 18-byte per-player score rows. $9EE8 selects the player's base for hole accounting. The printer reads the row directly at $68E0.
Four low bytes of player totals through hole nine. $9B7B stores the totals and $9D51 reads them for the on-screen subtotal.
Four high bytes paired with $5F88. $9B81 stores accumulated carries from the front-nine sum.
Four low bytes stored by $9B68 when the score summation reaches hole index 8 and separates the back nine.
Four high bytes paired with $5F90. $9B6E saves the carries before the front-nine accumulator is reset.

Base of four ranking slots. The scorecard counts competitors for each slot and the next-hole routine copies the new orders to $5FCC.

Current round's accumulating par low byte. $9B3A adds the hole par before saving it and passing the carry to the high byte.

Player slot used by the scoring, ranking and rendering loops. $9B4A starts it at the last active player.
Hole cursor used for indexing the selected player's stroke record. The back-nine draw starts it at nine.
High accumulator for carries out of the sum in A. $9EAE adds the current carry into it without replacing the caller's A.
High bytes of glyph table bases indexed by $8E and copied into the operand at $1248.
Low bytes of glyph table bases indexed by $8E and copied into the operand at $1242.

High byte of the play status panel glyph stream at $E2A8. $1FC3 loads it for the lower twelve rows.
