Computes cup distance and bearing from $83/$0D65 and $84/$44. $9372–$9375 save the distance word followed by the scaled-distance word after choosing the display scale.
The initial low view coordinate from $9365. $29F5 loads it for the active player when setting up a hole.
Low byte of the initial distance copied into the player's record by $A363 if the player has yet to take a stroke.
High byte of the initial distance read by $A366. This accompanies the low field at $937D in the unplayed position.
Low byte of the scaled cup distance after the copy at $9375. The distance display path also writes its calculated yardage here at $1B5D.
High byte of the scaled cup distance after the copy at $9375. The display path can replace it at $1B62 with the table index used for the three decimal digit adjustments.
Uses the high and low distance bytes to select a display scale and divisor of 1, 12 or 36. Saves the scaled value and scale index.
Returns unchanged if the incoming N flag is clear. With N set, complements Y:X and adds one plus incoming carry while propagating the carry from the low addition into Y.
Computes and projects marker endpoints around the ball. Uses a short path for lower skill levels in the default terrain state and draws a series of slope segments on the alternate path.
Projects a pair of height endpoints and draws their screen segment. Saves screen coordinates for the selected indicator row.
Five row values populated by $94B4. The strip testers compare the current or projected position's row against the indexed value.
Five lower column endpoints populated by $949B. A tested column strictly below the selected endpoint fails.
Five upper column endpoints populated by $94B9. A tested column greater than or equal to the selected endpoint fails.
Stores A in $AE. If A is nonzero and putting flag $8F is clear, adds the low bit of $0DC8.
Starts at zero when clearing round state. $95A2 selects the current marker slot and $95A7 advances it for subsequent range shots.
Sixteen offset bytes selected by the low nibble of $0DC8. The setup at $9574 multiplies the chosen byte by four and stores the resulting word at $2A23/$2A24.
Fetches the first player's two saved cup-coordinate bytes from $0D93 and $2A19 and tail-calls the cup rotation.
Fills eleven 240-byte bitmap strips, installs five object coordinates and draws the fixed set of terrain objects for the range view.
Five low bytes of the range background objects' X coordinates. $968C copies them to the terrain coordinate column.
Five high bytes paired with the table at $96B5, copied by $9692.
Copies eighteen bytes from $96EC to $96DA, wrapping the destination at 18. The initial offset is the low two bits of $0DC8.
Eighteen workspace bytes populated by $96BF. The indexed read at $A828 copies one entry to $0D69 for the vertical endpoint adjustment.
Source vector for the eighteen-byte wrapped copy at $96C7.
Uses the demo stage at $3A and shot index at $F1 to choose virtual stick commands. Advances through club selection, aim, fire and timing checks and writes the synthetic stick value at $81.
The demo copies a branch opcode from the shot table at $9790. The branch tests the comparison with the scripted aim coordinate and either starts the swing or continues steering.
On the zero branch, advances the demo step at $3A and sets synthetic input $81 to $10. Otherwise copies the scripted input byte from $97A1.
Target clubs 5, 9 and 12 for shot indices 0–2. While the club differs, the demo writes the synthetic input at $978D.
The synthetic down input used at $9722 while the selected club differs from the demonstration target.
Three branch opcodes installed at $973B in demo state 2. The captured values are all BEQ, so equality advances past the aiming phase.
Demo aim comparisons for three shots. State 2 compares the low aim coordinate with the chosen byte before selecting further stick motion or fire.
Synthetic horizontal stick bits written by $9740 when the state-2 aim branch does not take the fire path.
Three exact timer tick targets. A match at $9750 clears synthetic fire and advances the demo phase.
Three lower bounds on the timer tick for the synthetic snap press. At $9762 the routine accepts equality or greater.
$9773 installs this opcode at $977B for state five, before comparing aim against the retry target.
At $9778 the scripted state-five path compares the low aim position against this value.
While the retry aim branch at $977B falls through, this byte is copied to the demo joystick at $9780.
The scripted play state at $1F1C compares its progression index with this value.
Multiplies X and Y using the shared multiply workspace at $5B–$60, returning the product low byte in A and high byte in X.
Selects current ball, reference height or aim coordinates with X, or uses the overhead projection when $0D97 is set. Returns screen X in X, screen Y in Y and off-screen flags in A.
Forces a zero before the branch at $98F1 and returns. Its skipped path at $98F4 would put $68 into $3638 and $3639.
Shift-and-add multiplies the two words at $5B–$5C and $5F–$60 over 16 steps, leaving the 32-bit product in $5B–$5E.
Sign of a signed word product, derived by XOR of the multiplier and multiplicand high bytes. A negative result at $9950 selects the two's-complement path.
Converts both 16-bit operands to magnitudes, multiplies them and negates the four-byte product when their original signs differ.
Divides the word at $63–$64 by the word at $61–$62 using sixteen shift-and-subtract iterations. Returns quotient at $63–$64, remainder at $65–$66 and carry set for zero divisor.
Performs sixteen restoring-division steps using the divisor in $61/$62 and the work register at $63–$66. Returns carry set for a zero divisor.
Quotient sign from the XOR of dividend and divisor high bytes. The integrator preserves it around its nested division.
Original dividend high byte. Its sign is retained for signed remainder adjustment after the unsigned divide.

Records operand signs, divides their magnitudes, and gives the quotient the sign of the operand XOR and the remainder the sign of the dividend. On zero divisor it clears quotient and remainder and returns carry set.
Prepares a signed 32-bit dividend at $63–$66 and a signed 16-bit divisor at $61–$62 for the shared division loop. Returns via the common sign restoration path.
Multiplies unsigned A by 42, returns the product's high byte in A, and restores X and Y.
Pauses play display setup, disables sprites, draws the scorecard background and totals the hole. Walks the players backward to draw names, totals, front and back scores and par comparison marks.
Sets the panel font and builds all 25 rows of the setup bitmap and colour layout using the three template passes.
Writes colour 7 at column three and uses the one-based hole number to colour the selected hole. Writes $20 at column three before drawing the matching marker through the same helper.
Records the hole strokes and accumulates par. Sums score bytes separately for the front and back nine for each configured player, keeping the carry in a separate high byte.
Reads the eight glyphs in the selected player's name record and draws them from column five on the current scorecard row.
Compares the player's 16-bit score with accumulated par. Displays the magnitude with the over or under sign glyph, or an even-par glyph on equality.
For rounds after the first, lays out previous round totals from the low and high tables at $5F98 and $5F9C. Converts each to decimal before drawing it.
Adds $C4 to the round selector at $0D50 and stores the resulting low and high addends into the address operands at $9D01 and $9D00.
Low operand of the absolute glyph lookup at $9CFF, patched by $9CFC when selecting round text.
High operand of the absolute glyph lookup at $9CFF, patched by $9CF7. The loaded glyph value is shifted for the following bitmap calculation.
Draws front-nine strokes for the selected golfer from the card table, stopping at the current hole or at the nine-hole subtotal.
Draws back-nine strokes and totals for the selected golfer once the hole index is at least nine.
Walks the recorded strokes through the current hole, compares each to its par byte and writes colour pairs for under-par or over-par scores.
Eighteen entries indexed by hole number. $1992 copies the current hole header byte $C557 into this table before the scorecard uses it for the stroke comparison at $9E09.
Scans players by score rank at $5FC0. Assigns successive ordering slots at $5FC4 in player index order within a tie, then copies the assignments back to $5FC0.
Walks four player slots in descending order. Uses $9EE8 to get each record pointer and stores that slot's $5FC8 value at the current index $7E.
Increments the high accumulator byte at $5FD4 only if carry was set. Returns with the caller's A restored.
Takes the player index from $5FD2, looks up the player's display rank in $5FC0 and returns the corresponding row in X from $A11A.
Preserves the glyph in A while selecting the bitmap row with $1298. $1287 positions the cursor. The shared path at $9EC8 can also draw at the existing cursor and then advances it by eight bytes.
Writes the blank code ten to $A13E and to leading zero entries in $A13F–$A141. Returns at the first occupied entry.
Begins a pointer on page $5F at offset $40. Sets the immediate record length at $9EFA to $12 before advancing to the selected player.
Low immediate operand of the addition at $9EF9. Each iteration adds the patched stride to the record pointer, carries into $FA and decrements the player index until the address can be stored at $F9.
Selects the player name base at $A11E, sets the stride to eight and shares the indexed pointer arithmetic at $9EF4.
Forms eight times X plus the player slot at $5FD2. Returns the index in X and preserves A.
Loads X with $10 and returns because A is forced to zero at $9F35. The skipped path at $9F3A writes zero to the IRQ vector high byte and $F0 to $39.
Repeatedly divides by 1000, 100 and 10 to split the 16-bit value at $63–$64 into the four digit bytes at $A13F–$A142.
Selects X=0 and skips the X=1, 2 and 3 alternatives using overlapping BIT instructions.
Selects X=1 at the alternate entry in the operand of the BIT at $9F8C.
Selects X=2 inside the operand at $9F8F before the last overlapping BIT.
Sends offsets three and four of the score field at $A13E to the bitmap glyph writer in order.
Calls the name display helper, which returns early on the driving range. Sets the active golfer's panel marker and renders the configured players' stroke counts.
When $0D7D is zero, converts the active golfer's eight stored name characters to slot 3 glyph indices, draws them inverted in the right panel and writes the corresponding screen colour cells.
Looks up the glyph, flips every bit in its eight bitmap bytes and writes them to the chosen destination. Advances the text cursor after the copy.
For a nonzero player flag at $0D0D plus $5FD2, finds matrix row eight plus the player index and writes colour pair $3C to columns $21 and $22.
Increments the selected player's per-hole count up to the $32 limit and redraws the count in the player's panel row.
Uses $DB as a circular offset into the 90-byte glyph buffer at $0CA0. Copies a 30-cell slice via $0C40, which temporarily holds the source for the 90-byte copy back to $0CA0.
Converts the zero-based hole index to display digits and renders them with par read through the hole header pointer at $C557.
Low operand of the LDA at $A109. $A103 patches it from X after obtaining the hole header address.
High operand patched by $A106. The indexed hole header lookup supplies the address for the absolute load at $A109, whose byte is drawn by $9EC8.
Four bitmap rows indexed by player display rank at $9EBB, with four rows between adjacent players.
The new-game loop at $1534 fills 32 bytes with the internal space code $0A. The saved tee has $30,$1E,$2A followed by spaces.
First glyph slot in the score field. The output loop starts here when X is zero, and initialization can place a blank into this position.
Thousands score digit from the first division in the decimal splitter, saved at $9F51 before dividing the remainder by 100.
Hundreds score digit from the divide by 100, originally stored at $9F69.
Tens score digit saved from the quotient of the last divide by ten at $9F81.
Units score digit from the remainder of the final divide, saved at $9F86.
Score field suffix glyph. The stroke comparison selects glyph $0C or $0D for the signed difference display.
Draws the player setup screen, invokes the prompt and normal name and round entry, then initializes player records.
Uses successive rows 6–19 to draw the three parts of the setup panel with three pairs of values from the $5FE5–$5FFE parameter area.
Zeros the CIA time-of-day counters before polling keys at the player count prompt.
Enters the demo on D or when the time-of-day minute reaches one. Shift+Return invokes course selection, R enters the range and G the practice green. Digits 1–4 save a zero-based player count.
Disables VIC interrupts and sprites, banks in the KERNAL, masks CIA1 interrupts and stops its timers before calling SETLFS for device 8, secondary address $FF.
Calls $A252 to prepare disk and KERNAL state, then passes length three and the filename address $A2A1 to $A289 in A and Y:X.
Calls SETNAM with the supplied length and filename pointer, then LOAD. Stores the carry-set result in $A2A4, reinstalls the game IRQ and leaves RAM visible under the KERNAL.
The course load's three-byte name. The selection code supplies the first byte before passing the name ending CT to the loader.
Load failure flag. $A28E clears it before LOAD and $A296 increments it on a carry-set return.
Writes zero to CIA1 hours, minutes, seconds and tenths in that order.
Clears per-hole state, including each selected player's stroke count and saved-position flag. Sets the per-player state at $0D11 to two.
Writes zeros to $0D00–$0DC8.
Starts at player slot three and stores each slot's own index at $5FCC,X and $5FC0,X, calling $0E03 between slots.
Zeroes 88 bytes beginning at $5F40, calls $0E03, then clears per-hole player state through $A2B4.
Masks IRQs and waits for raster line $2C, then clears bits seven and four of $D011 before re-enabling IRQs.
Masks IRQs while waiting at raster line $2C. Clears bit seven of $D011, sets the display enable bit and re-enables IRQs.
Reads a key and returns unless it is PETSCII slash. On slash, pops six stack bytes, disables sprites and jumps to the setup entry at $1548.
Sets the current player's stroke count to one and copies the initialization byte from $0DA8 to both saved position fields at $0D15 and $0D19 for that player.
For the active player at $87, copies the starting coordinate bytes at $937D/$937E to $0D15,X and $0D19,X only if the stroke count at $0D0D,X is zero.
Compares players' hole stroke counts to make ranks, breaks ties with their previous order and clears the hole counters once the order has been saved.

Looks for a golfer who has yet to take the first shot and matches the current honours rank. Then compares distance fields among golfers who are still in play. Advances the hole if the completion flags are all set.
Uses A times 64 to select the prompt and draws four 16-glyph rows.
Four-by-sixteen layout for the player number and name prompt in the setup glyph encoding. Blank cells use $94.
Four-by-sixteen layout for Professional, Amateur and Kids.
Four-by-sixteen layout for F1, F3, F5 and F7 and their corresponding hole counts.

Reads names for the configured player slots, allows up to eight letters or spaces and handles Delete and Return. Commits the eight encoded values to the current player's record and calls the skill prompt before moving on.
Eight values for the name being entered. Letters A–Z are stored as 30–55 and a space as 10.
Four skill bytes selected by a player index. The menu maps K to zero, A to one and P to two before storing at $A657.
Runs $0E03 three times per inner count, with 32 inner iterations for each of 32 outer iterations.
Polls for P, A or K, translates to 2, 1 or 0 and saves the result in the current player skill table. Slash returns to setup.
Draws the round-length choices and waits for F1, F3, F5 or F7. Saves the chosen zero-based round count at $0D0B.
Positions the bitmap glyph cursor at row seven and draws glyph $17, followed by glyph $97 plus the selected player index at $5FD2.
Renders the prompt player digit from the work byte at $3B plus glyph offset $97.
Writes A to sixteen consecutive screen matrix cells on each of four rows, starting at $6124, $614C, $6174 and $619C.
Selects column ten and uses $0D67 plus sixteen as the row. Increments $0D68 and uses its low bit to alternate glyphs $94 and $95.
Clears four rows of sixteen screen-matrix and colour RAM cells and writes zeros to the corresponding four 128-byte bitmap portions.

Negates the active player's view coefficients from $2A19 and $0D93 into A and $43 and applies the selected course offsets at $A80E. Clears the two panel line origin offsets before preparing the projected endpoints.
Projects the wind reference vector and draws the indicator. Uses the selected wind magnitude and direction to compute the two horizontal components kept at $A877–$A87A.
Writable immediate operand for the first line drawing mode. The wind panel caller temporarily writes 1 here before restoring zero.

Adds either the hole byte at $C558 or the table byte indexed by $7E at $A82F to A and stores the result in $42. The same selector takes $0D69 from $C559 or $96DA. The line path subtracts $0D69 to place its second vertical endpoint.
Eighteen bytes indexed by $7E at $A823 and added to the horizontal offset at $42 when $0D1D is set.
Once per shot for a selector below two, adds signed two-byte adjustments from $A877–$A87A to the X and Z motion pairs. Sets its applied flag at $0DAF.
Low first shot adjustment byte added to $0D49 at $A854 and to the active velocity at $3A42.
High first shot adjustment byte. $A85D adds it to the first saved velocity's high byte with carry from $A854.
Low third-axis shot adjustment byte added to $0D4A at $A867.
High third-axis adjustment byte added with carry at $A870 before saving the component.
Computes offsets from the active player's saved position, enables the wind value only for skill 2 and updates the status panel geometry.
Clears the coordinate integration flag, repositions sprite 6 and switches it to pointer $99. Uses the terrain and state flags to choose whether to display the sprite and clears the shot flag.
When $0D51 requests the sequence, advances sprite 6's pointer unless the one-shot guard at $0DAF is set. On pointer $9D the routine runs the sprite state changes and clears the request.
Clears the generated sprite workspace from $6640 through $677F, then selects one of four sparse patterns using height cutoffs of 10, 15 and 20.
Copies 33 bytes into sparse offsets starting from $6680 using the paired tables at $A9C1 and $A9E9.
Uses 24 offset and value entries from $AA11 and $AA2E to draw the second height-dependent shape.
Uses 15 entries from $AA4B and $AA5D for the third height-dependent shape.
Uses seven offset and value pairs from $AA6F and $AA79 for the smallest silhouette.
The first 33 entries give the offsets written by $A981 relative to $6680. Offsets at or above 64 select the second cell.
The first 33 entries are byte values for the offset entries at $A9C1. $A987 reads them in descending index order.
The first 24 entries map each byte from $AA2E to an offset from $6680. The last five bytes before the value table are beyond the loop bound at $A991.
The first 24 entries supply sprite bytes indexed in tandem with $AA11. The descending copy starts at index 23. The last five bytes before the next offset table are outside that copy.
The first fifteen entries specify the destination positions for $A9A1, relative to $6680. The three bytes at the end fall outside that loop's index range.
The first fifteen entries give the sparse byte values for offsets in $AA4B. The final three bytes are outside the descending copy at $A9A1.
Sparse destination offsets used by the loop at $A9B3 for the smallest sprite variant. The loop indexes seven pairs from 6 to 0.
Sparse byte values paired with the offsets at $AA6F. $A9BA writes them into the smallest height-scaled sprite.
SID preset column of frequency low values. The staged preset loader reads it at $AB29.
SID preset column of frequency high values, indexed at $AB2F before writing the per-voice frequency workspace.
SID preset column of pulse width low bytes, copied by $AB35 and $AB38.
SID preset column of pulse width high bytes, read at $AB3B.
SID preset column of waveform control values, read at $AB41 for the selected effect.
SID preset column of attack and decay values. The effect loader reads it at $AB47 before staging the envelope.
Offset six into the eight-byte SID preset records. Indexed by preset times eight at $AB4D to obtain the last parameter copied into the voice state.
Walks through SID offsets 24 down to 0 and zeros every write register.
Clears SID, sets the volume and filter defaults, and applies the initial cutoff.
Sets both frequency registers to zero for all three SID voices.
Copies seven bytes from preset Y at $AA83 plus eight times Y into the synthesis fields for voice X. Preserves X.
Three per-voice frequency low bytes staged by $AB2C and read at $ABDA when triggering the voice.
Three frequency high bytes, loaded into the selected voice at $ABE3. $AC69 can override the first entry for a swing sound phase.
Three pulse width low bytes. $ABE6 reads the selected voice's entry for the write at $ABE9.
High portions of the three voice pulse widths, transferred by $ABEC and $ABEF.
Three waveform control bytes staged at $AB44. $AC01 writes the selected voice's control value before the gate is set.
Three envelope attack and decay bytes loaded at $ABF2 before the selected voice's attack-decay register write.
Three envelope sustain and release bytes transferred to SID at $ABFB during voice trigger.
Low SID filter cutoff workspace. The filter setter reads it at $ABC0 for the write to $D415.
High cutoff workspace. $ABBA keeps the adjusted high cutoff just before writing it to $D416.
Filter resonance and voice-routing shadow. The voice routing helpers change bits zero through two before writing it to $D417.
SID mode and volume shadow. $AB7D reads it for the write to $D418.
Saved SID voice index. $ABA8 subtracts it from eight times the index to compute the seven-register voice stride.
Signed high cutoff adjustment. The cutoff routine at $ABAD selects the positive or negative saturation path from its sign.
Current swing-effect phase. The raster sound logic uses it to choose an intermediate frequency or terminate the effect.
Sets bit zero in the cached SID routing byte at $AB6D and writes it to $D417. Copies the mode and volume byte at $AB6E to $D418.
Selects filter-route bit 1 before joining the common filter register write.
Selects filter-route bit 2 before joining the common filter register write.
Clears filter-route bit 0 before joining the filter register write.
Masks the SID routing byte with $FD through $AB90 to clear the voice-two routing bit while preserving the others.
Uses $FB at $AB90 to clear the voice-three filter routing bit, then updates the SID registers through the shared writer.
Saves the input voice index X at $AB6F and returns seven times that index in Y.
Adds the signed adjustment at $AB70 to A with saturation at 0 or 255, writes the result to the SID cutoff high byte and copies the low byte from $AB6B.
Selects the SID voice with register offset seven times X. Loads frequency, pulse width, ADSR and control from per-voice tables before setting the waveform's gate bit.
Computes the SID voice register offset, clears the gate bit from its stored control value and writes the control register.
Resets the voice state through $AB72, copies preset zero into voice zero and applies its registers. Sets sequence state one and queues value five in timer slot ten.
Stores the countdown byte in $0DB9,X and $0D98,X. Marks timer slot X active through $0DA9,X.
Advances the sequence in $AB71 when its timer at $0DB3 expires. Triggers voice 1 with the next high frequency byte from $AC77, or clears the sequence and frequency at $04.
Indexed by the sound phase minus two at $AC66. $AC69 installs the result for SID voice one's frequency high byte.
Once the swing timer reaches $1B with no active sequence at $AB71, sets sequence state four, configures the filter and starts voice 1 with preset one.
Calls $AB96, copies preset two into voice index one through $AB22 and applies the voice registers through $ABD2.
Calls $AB72 to update filter routing, copies preset three into voice index zero and applies its SID registers.
Configures filter and routing, loads presets four through six into the three voices and retriggers them from voice 3 back to voice 1.
Sets $AB6E to $4F, derives another SID control from height through $AD17 and applies preset seven to voice zero.
Subtracts eight from $E4 with a floor of zero, shifts the result left twice and uses $7F when the byte has its sign bit set. Adds $80, stores it at $AB6F and updates the SID through $ABAD.
Called by the menu keyboard reader when GETIN returns a nonzero key. Calls $AB96, loads preset eight for voice index one and sends it to the SID.
Sets up and gates on voice 2, starts timer slot ten, waits for the countdown and releases the gate.
Clears the sort and clipping work arrays, then repeatedly finds the deepest unprocessed point. Saves the ordered indices at $0AC0 and projects each object.
Working projected depth column index. The terrain scan initializes it at $AD7B and advances it at $ADD8.
Skips points at insufficient depth or off screen. Projects the terrain object, selects the width tier and composites its canopy and companion masks at the resulting position.
Temporarily exposes RAM under I/O, scans one terrain shape mask, and combines selected source bits into the destination bitmap with the masks at $52 and $53.
Converts projected depth to a tier index with descending thresholds. For nearer tiers it uses the low bit of $ED to choose one of two neighbouring masks.
Reads the mask base from the low and high pointer tables, advances by strip index times strip width and returns the source bit mask for the remaining column offset.
Loads $C900 into the pointer at $FB–$FC.
Records projected shape bounds in one of two groups of screen-coordinate arrays, using the shape's type index and current render coordinates.

Checks clipping and state flags before walking the sorted course records. Compares ball depth and height with candidate objects, calls the overlap tests and updates $0D54 and the current collision state.
Reads the bitmap colour pair under the ball, then checks its four neighbours for the uniform-colour case and records a separate result code for it.
Samples the pixel under sprite 7 and checks neighbouring colours to distinguish the uniformly coloured case.

With X equal to the object index at $DD, tests the ball pixel in $0D41 and $0D40 against two rectangles. Minimum edges are inclusive and maximum edges are exclusive. Writes Boolean results to $0D33 and $0D32.
Entry through the BIT operand at $B280. Loads zero when the ball pixel falls outside the first bounds test.
Loads zero for an out-of-range coordinate in the second ball pixel rectangle test.
Tests the shadow pixel in $0D53 and $0D44 against the same two indexed rectangles as $B25C. Writes the first result to $0D2B and the second to $0D29.
Loads zero when the first shadow rectangle excludes the shadow pixel.
Loads zero before saving the second shadow rectangle result for an out-of-range shadow pixel.
Updates launch velocity on the first object-contact path selected in $B03D. Uses the current input and collision record to set the post-contact velocity fields.
Clamps the forward velocity used for the rebound, converts a quarter of it to signed lateral velocity according to which side of the object the ball reached, and clears snap and wind adjustments.
Index of the most recently handled course object, saved at $B3CA and compared at $B124 during the later contact test.
Tests display bounds, swing phase and ground height before dispatching the terrain response. The stop path clears velocity integration and hides sprite 7.
Samples several positions near the recorded ball pixel to choose the ground transition result returned in carry.
With IRQs masked, shifts $3E right and rotates its outgoing bit into $E7. Clears the four motion bytes at $A877–$A87A and re-enables IRQs.
While interrupts are masked, halves the unsigned $3E/$E7 component and shifts the signed $3C/$E5 and $3D/$E6 components with sign extension. Clears the four stored shot adjustment bytes.
Independently encoded copy of the three component shift and adjustment reset at $B4DE. Its IRQ mask covers all three updates.
Compares depth against the pin position and checks position and terrain around it. Updates the two high collision-state bits at $0D26.
Enters the ball-position strip tester with X=4 and its exclusive loop bound set to 5.

Scans entries zero through three. Returns carry set when the high position byte at $0D41 matches the strip and the low byte at $0D40 is within the inclusive lower and exclusive upper limits. The entry at $B5CD selects strip four alone.
Exclusive stop index used by the comparison at $B5F3. $B5D8 patches it to limit the coordinate test to the requested strips.
Enters the projected-coordinate strip tester with X=4 and its exclusive loop bound set to 5.
Tests the corresponding strip bounds using high byte $0D53 and low byte $0D44. Starts at strip zero and programs the compare at $B61F to stop after strip three.
Exclusive strip index endpoint patched at $B604 and tested by CPX at $B61F.
Calls the prior contact adjustment twice, then clears both signed lateral velocities under IRQ masking and sets $0D27.
Resets $0D28, the lateral-motion stop flag at $0D27 and the movement state at $0D01.
Iterates over two 48-byte bitmap areas. Uses the source strip at $204A for position-specific substitutions where the old pixel matches the tested colour pair.

During timing phase 3 after tick $2A, checks whether the snap landed in the allowed interval for the current skill and terrain. On the exceptional branch, restores reference coordinates and sets the one-shot flag.
Tests the multicolour pixel at X $3C and Y $BE, and conditionally the line above. Saves one of three outcomes at $0D04.
When $0D01 equals one, changes it to two, clears $0D07, sets $0D06 to twelve and calls $37C0.

For X equal to zero, scans the current bitmap row one cell at a time for a pixel whose two colour bits differ in the masked region. At the end of the row it discards its return address to skip the caller's processing.
Walks the projected depth columns at ($FC) and ($FE) for this polygon's vertex count. Keeps the smallest unsigned 16-bit value in $EF/$F0 and returns its high byte.
Forms five times the hole index and adds the quotient of the active golfer angle's high byte shifted up eight bits divided by $02D8. Wraps the combined offset to keep it within ninety cells.
Uses the row in $FF to find colour RAM and writes colour 5 to columns 0–29.
Looks up the matrix colour byte for the row at $B802 and fills its first thirty cells.
Five screen matrix fill bytes indexed by the display row at $B7F7. The row fill writes the chosen value to the first 30 columns.
Copies ninety bytes from ($FB) into the glyph buffer at $0CA0.
Copies the first thirty bytes of the current glyph row to the supplied indirect destination.
Selects a 90-byte glyph stream, copies it to the working table, shifts its display window and refreshes the panel.

Displays the course prompt, accepts A–Z and stores the selected letter at $A2A1 for the CT filename.
Uses X to select a sixteen-glyph string at $B8A9 and writes it into the play bitmap using the text bank selected by $8E = 3.
Sixteen-glyph prompt rows. The first four read NEW COURSE Y/N, INPUT COURSE, TURN DISK and ERROR RETRY Y/N.

Fills the 128-byte strip from $5BE0 to $5C5F with zero.
Accepts Y or N after a round. Y opens the filename-letter prompt and loads the chosen course table. Slash transfers directly to round reset.
Polls the keyboard for a PETSCII letter A through Z and saves it as the first byte of the course table filename at $A2A1.
Selects DMO, RNG or a three-byte disk name from the course filename table according to the demo, practice and hole flags. Calls the shared named load routine.
Two adjacent three-byte filenames. DMO is selected for the demo and RNG for the driving range.
Chooses the leading letter from the demo, practice or per-hole course state. Writes the letter to $B9C9 and passes the three-byte buffer with its existing TF suffix to the shared loader.
Range override for the first letter of a TF filename. The range path uses this byte at $B9B0 when it is nonzero.
Demo path's TF filename prefix override, tested at $B9A6 before checking the range and per-hole selectors.
Three-character TF load name. $B9BA writes the terrain bank letter before the loader uses this address.
Clears and recolours the first 30 cells of the course header. Translates PETSCII letters, digits and spaces from $BEE0 to the bitmap font and draws each glyph inverted.
Polls Y or N before requesting PRNT. Retries a failed load on Y, and jumps to $6800 after success.
Branches to the printer retry prompt on carry set. Falls through to RTS on success.
Calls the named disk loader with a four-byte filename, PRNT, pointed to by $BA92.
PETSCII filename requested by the scorecard print branch.
Visits each object from the last down to zero, projects its coordinate columns, halves the projected X for bitmap pixels and calls $BACA with the result in $40/$41.
Uses $40/$41 as a reference pixel, applies the clear mask at two points, then writes the masked colour from $52 to three adjacent points.
Reads the bitmap byte at ($FD),Y, ANDs it with the preserve mask at $53 and writes it back.
Applies preserve mask $53 to the destination at ($FD),Y, ORs in the replacement bits at $52 and stores the result.
Loads X from $40 and Y from $41. Decrements the returned Y by one.
Projects thirteen points starting at X $0400 and Z $0500, advancing Z by $0708 per point. Alternates two bitmap byte patterns from $BB48.
Two alternating bitmap byte patterns for the projected dotted reference. $BB2D selects between them using the low bit of the marker counter.
Base of the interleaved pointers to each polygon's X-low column. $2104 reads the low destination address for the cumulative X stores.
The high bytes of the interleaved destination pointers whose low bytes start at $BB4A. $210A selects a polygon's pointer and patches the indexed X low-byte store.
Base of the interleaved pointers to each polygon's X-high column. $2110 reads its low destination address byte.
The high-byte column of the interleaved pointers to each polygon's X high-byte array. Read at $2116 to patch the store at $2159.
Base of interleaved pointers to the polygon Y-low columns. $211C supplies the low address for the indexed Y store.
The high-byte column of the interleaved pointers to each polygon's Y low-byte array. Read at $2122 for the store at $2170.
Base of interleaved pointers to the polygon Y-high columns, indexed at $2128.
The high-byte column of the interleaved pointers to each polygon's Y high-byte array. The polygon decoder reads this through $212E and writes it to $217E.
Eight vertex counts populated from the hole stream at $20F7. The edge-processing routines use the selected count to bound a polygon traversal.
Low bytes of terrain object X coordinates. $2233 scatters the four-byte disk records into separate columns, and the projection and collision code use these indexed coordinates.

In the boundary decoder's workspace layout, this is the high byte column paired with the $BB92 boundary X low bytes. The terrain object layout reuses the address range as part of its wider X-low column.
Lower bytes of the boundary decoder's second coordinate. This address is also interior to the terrain object X-low column after the workspace is reused.
High bytes of the second boundary coordinate in the workspace layout selected by the decoder at $2100. The terrain object decoder reuses the same RAM.
High bytes paired with the object X column at $BB92. $224F writes this column when it unpacks terrain records.
Object Z low bytes loaded at $2255. Sorting uses these bytes to compare objects whose Z high bytes tie.
High bytes of object Z. This is the first coordinate byte used by the depth sort comparison at $AD92.

Uses the option byte at $8F to select the X/Y pair 5/5 or 9/10. In the second case A is set to 12 before storing the motion parameter at $0D3B.

Eighteen three-byte names indexed by hole number, from A01 through A18 in the captured state. Success of the custom loader determines which disk files need to exist literally.
One filename prefix per hole for TF loads. In the captured Cypress Creek state, all eighteen prefixes are A.
Banks out I/O with $01 = $24 and copies twelve pages from $C000–$CBFF to $D000–$DBFF. Re-enables I/O with $01 = $25 before enabling interrupts.

Width or stride in bytes of a mask strip, indexed by the selected terrain mask.
Counts and values at the start of the selected hole record. The boundary decoder reads the per-group counts here.
Par byte in the decoded hole record. The round loop reads it at $198F and the header draw reads it at $A109.

Low origin offset subtracted from the descriptor coordinate at $228A before dividing the relative coordinate by twelve.

Count of four-byte course records unpacked by $2233 into four coordinate columns.

Saves the high zero-page workspace, copies the SETNAM filename, and dispatches the resident printer or course request. Numbered holes normally rewrite to the course's 00 file and select a stream number before the drive transfer.
Hides ROM and I/O, copies four pages from $DC00–$DFFF and two from $FB00–$FCFF into $6800–$6DFF, then joins loader cleanup.
Immediate byte of ADC at $CC97, part of the requested numbered-hole stream calculation. Saves the stream index in $F1 before rewriting two filename digits at $CD57/$CD58.
Prepares the rewritten filename and raster-sensitive transfer parameters, then sends the name to the drive via CIA2.
Reads the stream header and expands successive packed streams until the requested stream count is exhausted, then drains the transfer.
Restores the saved stack position and port, waits for the drive signal, then updates the course title for CT requests and joins loader cleanup.
Immediate value of the LDX at $CD2A. The loader puts $EF in the stack pointer, pulls the memory configuration, waits for bit six of CIA2 port A and switches to $38 before dispatch.
Restores the sixteen saved zero-page bytes at $F0–$FF and returns through the status instruction at $CD54.
Clears carry on the success exit after restoring the saved zero page bytes.

Third byte of the loader's filename buffer at $CD56, overwritten at $CCA4 when selecting the base course file. The following bytes belong to the same fixed-length transmit buffer.
Sends a byte MSB first as eight data bits on CIA2's serial port and preserves the calling X and Y values.

Writes RTS ($60) over the LDA opcode at $CDCC. After the receive call returns, this makes the wrapper return before it can re-enable the store at $CE03.
Patches the response operand to two and the low byte of the indexed receive store to $60. Waits through $CDD1, branches on an incoming one and otherwise uses the received byte to patch $CE0E.

Waits for the drive and uses raster timing to avoid a bad-line transfer. Collects the serial bits through CIA2 port A and stores successive reconstructed bytes in the page $0500.
Immediate operand of SBC at $CDDA. The raster test waits when the subtraction is nonnegative and the result is a multiple of eight.
Immediate value at $CDE2. $CDE4 writes $22 to CIA2 port A, then $CDEA clears bit 5. The following timed reads combine successive samples of the port and write the resulting byte to $0500,Y.
Immediate $02 operand applied to the received byte at the end of the four CIA2 samples.
Writes the assembled data byte in A into the selected buffer at the current offset in Y. Briefly decrements and restores the border colour before advancing the index.
Immediate receive-loop end index. $CDC9 patches it from the first received byte before $CE0D compares Y on later passes.
Builds the variable-width length and offset tables and decodes literal bytes and prior-output back-references into the destination encoded in the stream.
Accumulates the requested number of bits, refilling the bit reservoir through the packed byte reader.
